description: Activate for OSS adoption work -- README conversion surfaces, quickstart, templates, release announcements, contributor funnel, story angles -- and any update to the maintained growth strategy at WIP/growth-strategy.md.

name: supply-chain-security
description: Activate when reviewing or modifying dependency resolution, lockfile schema, package downloaders, signature/integrity checks, file integration cleanup, or anything that could expose APM to dependency confusion, typosquatting, malicious packages, or token leakage.

name: coss
description: Helps implement coss UI components correctly. Use when building UIs with coss primitives (buttons, dialogs, selects, forms, menus, tabs, inputs, toasts, etc.), migrating from shadcn/Radix to coss/Base UI, composing trigger-based overlays, or troubleshooting coss component behavior. Covers imports, accessibility, Tailwind styling, and common pitfalls.

name: coss-particles
description: Index of all COSS UI particle examples. Use when implementing UI features to find copy-paste-ready component patterns built on coss primitives. Each particle has a description and a JSON URL for easy installation.

name: cognitive-doc-design
description: Design docs that reduce cognitive load. Trigger: writing guides, READMEs, RFCs, onboarding, architecture, or review-facing docs.

name: gentle-ai-chained-pr
description: Trigger: PRs over 400 lines, stacked PRs, review slices. Split oversized changes into chained PRs that protect review focus.

name: go-testing
description: Trigger: Go tests, go test coverage, Bubbletea teatest, golden files. Apply focused Go testing patterns.

name: yao-doc
description: Yao process documentation expert. ALWAYS invoke this skill when the user needs to discover available processes, read process signatures, or validate process names. Do not guess process APIs — use this skill first.

name: yao-process
description: Yao process execution expert. ALWAYS invoke this skill when the user needs to call a Yao process, query data models, run scripts, or check process permissions. Do not call processes without checking this skill first.

name: yao-web
description: Web information retrieval expert. ALWAYS invoke this skill when the user needs to search the web, fetch a URL, or access real-time information beyond training data. Do not guess or use stale knowledge — use this skill first.

name: hive.linkedin-automation
description: Read before automating LinkedIn with browser_* tools. LinkedIn combines shadow DOM (#interop-outlet), strict Trusted Types CSP that silently drops innerHTML, Lexical composer, native beforeunload dialogs that hang the bridge, and aggressive spam filters — each has bitten us at least once. Verified flows for profile messaging, connection-request acceptance, feed composition, and search. Requires hive.browser-automation. Verified against logged-in production 2026-04-11.

name: hive.x-automation
description: Read before automating X / Twitter with browser_* tools. Verified flows for post, reply, delete, search-and-engage, plus the Draft.js compose quirks that silently disable the send button. Includes the daily-reply and job-market-reply playbooks. Requires hive.browser-automation for the underlying screenshot + coordinate workflow. Verified 2026-04-11.

name: hive.context-preservation
description: Proactively extract critical values from tool results into working notes before automatic context pruning destroys them.

name: hive.error-recovery
description: Follow a structured recovery decision tree when tool calls fail instead of blindly retrying or giving up.

name: hive.note-taking
description: Maintain a free-form scratchpad of decisions, extracted values, and open questions so context pruning doesn't lose anything you still need.

name: hive.quality-monitor
description: Periodically self-assess output quality to catch degradation before the judge does.

name: bigquery-pipeline-audit
description: Audits Python + BigQuery pipelines for cost safety, idempotency, and production readiness. Returns a structured report with exact patch locations.

name: ai-prompt-engineering-safety-review
description: Comprehensive AI prompt engineering safety review and improvement prompt. Analyzes prompts for safety, bias, security vulnerabilities, and effectiveness while providing detailed improvement recommendations with extensive frameworks, testing methodologies, and educational content.

name: postgresql-code-review
description: PostgreSQL-specific code review assistant focusing on PostgreSQL best practices, anti-patterns, and unique quality standards. Covers JSONB operations, array usage, custom types, schema design, function optimization, and PostgreSQL-exclusive security features like Row Level Security (RLS).

name: create-skill
description: Create a new skill in the current repository. Use when the user wants to create/add a new skill, or mentions creating a skill from scratch. This skill follows the workflow defined in .agents/skills/README.md and helps scaffold, validate, and sync new skills.

name: vercel-react-best-practices
description: React and Next.js performance optimization guidelines from Vercel Engineering. This skill should be used when writing, reviewing, or refactoring React/Next.js code to ensure optimal performance patterns. Triggers on tasks involving React components, Next.js pages, data fetching, bundle optimization, or performance improvements.

name: twitter-algorithm-optimizer
description: Analyze and optimize tweets for maximum reach using Twitter's open-source algorithm insights. Rewrite and edit user tweets to improve engagement and visibility based on how the recommendation system ranks content.

name: recipe-front-adjust
description: Adjust an already-implemented UI in-session with verification against the design source

name: shipswift
description: ShipSwift skill library — 118 production-ready SwiftUI skills for iOS/macOS covering animations (view transitions, particle transitions, change effects, shimmer, confetti, typewriter, 28 Metal shaders), charts (line, bar, donut, radar, heatmap, 3D network graph), UI components (onboarding, alert, stepper, search bar, cached remote images) and full-stack modules (Cognito/Supabase auth, camera, chat, StoreKit subscriptions, CDK infra). Use when building SwiftUI features, adding animations/charts/components, or when the user mentions ShipSwift.

name: flow-next-resolve-pr
description: Resolve PR review feedback. Fetches unresolved threads, triages, fixes, replies and resolves via GraphQL. Use when asked to address review comments.

name: derive-tests
description: 'What should we test' or a coverage map: derive the coverage map and missing tests from docs and code; check mode reports staleness.

name: document-app
description: 'Document the app': write or refresh an app's system docs from its code. 'Are the docs right?': check mode, which only reports where docs and code disagree.

name: handover
description: Write the handover a fresh session starts from: the objective, what is true now, the evidence actually obtained, what is left, the open decisions and the next concrete action, reconciled with the disk first. Started by name only: /agent-harness:handover in Claude Code, $agent-harness:handover in Codex.

name: performance-audit-static
description: Only when a performance audit is asked for (ship-check asks by name; a release proposes, never runs it): static audit of N+1 queries, over-fetching, indexes, caching.

name: retro
description: Build a session's learnings into the setup: its friction, what went wrong and why, then an improved instruction, route, hook or script, verified, or 'no setup change warranted'. Started by name only: /agent-harness:retro in Claude Code, $agent-harness:retro in Codex.

name: security-audit-static
description: Only when a security audit is asked for (ship-check asks by name; a release proposes one, never runs it): a static audit of AI-built code against its documented trust boundaries.

name: ship-check
description: Is this safe to ship? Documents the app, wires the agent's context, runs the correctness, security and performance reviews and an independent unsteered pass, maps test coverage, and compiles one reviewer-ready shipping packet. Started by name only: /ai-shipping:ship-check in Claude Code, $ai-shipping:ship-check in Codex.

name: start-here
description: Where to start, and what comes next, along the product lifecycle: from a new idea, new evidence, an agreed change, a bug or a release to the next step and the skill that does it. Started by name only: /product:start-here in Claude Code, $product:start-here in Codex.

name: bama
description: Build any Mac app. Start here to pick the next skill for a native macOS app.

name: agent-cli
description: Optional command line and MCP server for a macOS app, so Claude Code, Codex, and scripts can drive it (list, add, change, search, act) through the running app. Use when the user wants agents to work with their app or its data, asks for a CLI, an MCP server, or automation for the app, or says "Claude should be able to use my app".

name: app-brief
description: One-page brief (docs/BRIEF.md) for a new macOS app, written before any code. Use when the user has an app idea, wants to replace an app they pay for, or the research and clone skills are done.

name: clone
description: Walk through any existing app (native Mac app with computer use, web app with a browser), screenshot every screen, menu, and dialog, write a screen index, and turn it into user stories. Use when the user wants to clone, rebuild, replace, or copy the design of an app, or says "screenshot every screen".

name: design-from-app
description: Rebuild the look of an app the user likes as a native SwiftUI design kit, by measuring its screenshots (sizes, spacing, type, colors, icons), building its parts, and comparing pixel by pixel until they match. Use when the user names an app whose look they want, shares screenshots of one, or says "make it look like X".

name: improve-loop
description: Autonomous loop that works through docs/STORIES.md one story at a time for a macOS app, building, snapshotting, comparing against reference screenshots, fixing, and committing, until a milestone is done. Use when the user says "keep going", "work through the backlog", "make it match the reference", or wants an unattended improvement loop.

name: new-mac-app
description: Create a native macOS SwiftUI app from a working template (Swift package, SwiftData, build script, icon script, snapshot mode, git), with no Xcode GUI. Use when the user wants to start a new Mac app or scaffold a macOS project.

declaredTools: Bash(*/new-app.sh *) Bash(git *) Bash(swift *) Read Write Edit

name: research
description: Online research for a macOS app before building it, run as parallel researcher subagents, saved to docs/research/. Use when the user asks what to build, which features matter, how the best apps in a category work, how a macOS API or integration works, or wants a feature comparison.

name: ux-design
description: UX pass for one feature of a macOS app, covering names, flow, where it opens (inline, popover, sheet, window, alert), states, words, hover help, accessibility, and AI features. Use before coding a story that adds a screen, an action, or text, when user-stories or improve-loop call it, or when the user asks for a UX review, clearer wording, better names, or whether something should be a modal.

name: remotion-video
description: Make a short video about a product or brand (promo, launch, explainer, demo or social clip) entirely in code with Remotion, from idea to a rendered MP4 with sound. The owner approves the idea and a storyboard before anything is built.

name: agami-query
description: Answers natural-language questions about the user's database. Loads the agami semantic model (subject areas, tables, columns, relationships with join cardinality, entities, metrics) and few-shot examples from <artifacts_dir>/<profile>/, generates SQL via the examples-first traversal (pick subject area → match examples → resolve entities/metrics → compound table context), executes it locally via the user's chosen tool (psql / mysql / snowsql / sqlite3 native CLI, DuckDB binary, or the Python driver `execute_sql.py` — which runs the scope gates and reports fan-trap/chasm-trap and aggregation findings on the receipt), returns results as a markdown table with optional CSV export, and renders Chart.js HTML charts on request. All execution is local — no data leaves the machine.

name: agami-save-correction
description: Saves a user correction so future queries learn from it. Always appends a (question, corrected_sql) pair to the subject area's example library under <artifacts_dir>/<profile>/prompt_examples/<area>/. Additionally, classifies the correction and — when applicable — applies a surgical edit to the semantic model itself (relationship fix, column metadata, or new metric) via the curation engine. Every model edit is validated before write; the validator is the binding gate, and a failed validation reverts. Shows the user a model diff for approval before any model mutation.

name: cc-safety-net
description: Operate CC Safety Net: explain why a command was blocked, triage false positives, configure custom rulebooks, manage agent CLI integrations, and diagnose protection.

name: dexpaprika-api
description: Access the DexPaprika API, CLI, and streaming service to query DEX data including networks, pools, tokens, and trading activity. Use this skill when making HTTP requests to api.dexpaprika.com or streaming.dexpaprika.com, or when using dexpaprika-cli for blockchain DEX information.

name: fxmacrodata
description: Macroeconomic releases, release calendars, and FX spot rates from official sources. Read-only. Trigger phrases: fxmacrodata, cpi release, inflation data, non-farm payrolls, policy rate, economic calendar, fx rate.

name: implement-spec-with-goal
description: Implement a spec using the harness's goal feature.

name: musedin
description: Read-only MusedIn data: open roles and job posts for AI agents, member profiles, the public feed, verification records. No key needed. Trigger phrases: musedin, agent jobs, jobs for my agent, find an agent, agent profile.

name: re0-git
description: Rewrite a finished commit's message into a clean, handoff-ready form in your own log style, and place a late commit in time order on a linear history, so `git log` alone tells the story. User-invoked: run it once you've decided to commit.

name: retro
description: Conduct a retrospective on a coding session.

name: chuhai-market-entry
description: Plan a Chinese company's entry into an overseas market (出海): choose the market with evidence, then plan entity, payments, localisation, compliance, channels and team for the first twelve months. Use when asked 出海计划, 我们要进入东南亚 / 中东 / 欧洲 / 美国市场, how should a Chinese company expand overseas, or a go-global plan. Produces a market scorecard, a twelve-month entry plan by workstream, the compliance and data checklist for the chosen market, and the top risks with mitigations. Bilingual output on request.

name: dedot
description: Review the middle dots (U+00B7) in a Korean passage, field, section, file or folder the writer names, and propose a per-dot replacement only where a dot strings together an open list, keeping every legitimate or protected dot and leaving the text unedited.

name: independent-idea-engine
description: Fierce autonomous internal co-founder. Bounded web research for evidence-backed improvements. Structured idea formulation with self-critique filter that rejects ideas not serving the goal. Auto-implements high-confidence aligned improvements, proposes medium-confidence ideas for approval. Evaluates viral coefficient, AI search visibility (GEO), and solo SaaS economics. Considers higher pursuits: employing disabled people, spiritual tech investigation, 99% wealth donation ethos.

name: whychk
description: Right after you pick an option, have a fresh outsider find the sharpest gap in the choice, then explain that gap in your own words, one gap at a time.

name: agami-reconcile
description: Reconciles known (label, expected_value) numbers from an existing dashboard against agami's answers. Input can be a SCREENSHOT of a Metabase / Power BI / Tableau / Looker dashboard (Claude's vision extracts the pairs), a CSV, or numbers pasted inline — the user doesn't need to know which; they can just ask. For each pair, the skill generates a matching NL question, runs it through the active profile's semantic model, diffs actual vs expected, and surfaces matches in green and mismatches in red with drill-down receipts. The strongest onboarding demo for a skeptical data engineer — either we agree with their numbers (trust earned via evidence) or we surface a real definitional disagreement (trust earned via transparency).

name: handoff-spec
description: Hand a spec that is mid-implementation to another machine or another agent.

name: audit-agents
description: Audit or rewrite AGENTS.md so it holds only lasting principles. Run it only when the user asks for it by name; never invoke it on your own.

name: re0-watch
description: Watch a long-running agent job for stalls and alert by default, with recovery only as a proposal a human approves.

name: dedash
description: Remove the em and en dashes an agent drops into running prose where a comma, colon, parentheses or a sentence break belongs, from a user-owned scope, keeping hyphens, ranges and dashes that separate a label from its text.

name: ios-simulator-skill
description: Build, test, and drive iOS apps in the Simulator with 30 token-efficient scripts. Use when asked to build or test an Xcode project, launch an app on a simulator, tap/type/swipe through its UI by accessibility label, take screenshots or visual diffs, audit accessibility, read logs or diagnose hangs, or manage simulators (boot, erase, permissions, location, push, appearance). macOS only; needs Xcode, Python 3.12+ and idb.

name: macrothink
description: User-invoked read-only pass for checking whether the current direction is tunnel-visioned: strip the session's bait, fan out 2 to 5 same-model fresh reads, and report divergence first without treating convergence as proof; or, when asked, re-read one decision at a larger scale and return linked expansions, a no-change, an abstain or a handoff.

name: multithink
description: Adjudicate already-collected independent reads of one artifact or question into findings classified by cited evidence alone, never by how many agreed, preserving every original, with one optional caller-run exchange that circulates only disputed citations and records each evidence-caused revision.

name: re0-import
description: Land handed-over material of any shape (a note, a link, a dump, a correction) in the document of an existing knowledge base that owns it: read the base's own routing documents first, edit in each document's own grammar, hash files before writing, and report what cannot be placed instead of guessing. User-invoked. Not for researching the subject or designing a new structure.

name: re0-squash
description: Republish a GitHub repository as one signed commit: squash its whole history into one commit with the same tree, then delete the remote and recreate it under the same name and settings, because a force push leaves the old commits reachable by hash, in forks and in pull requests. User-invoked, and the deletion cannot be undone.

name: re0-tutorial
description: Learn one skill of the suite through three graded levels whose completion rests on the learner's own submission, never on an invocation trace.

name: acceptable-use-policy-drafting
description:
Use this skill when a company needs rules for how staff use company systems, data, devices and AI
tools, or asks "write our acceptable use policy", "AUP for employees", "can staff use ChatGPT at
work", "AI usage policy", "BYOD rules", "remote work security rules" or "a policy people will
actually read". Finds how people really work (devices, apps, AI tools, travel), puts the choices
to the reader as decisions, drafts a short plain-language policy with concrete do and do not
examples, and adds a comprehension check and an acknowledgement text for onboarding.

name: access-review-campaign-prep
description:
Use this skill when a periodic user access review is due, an auditor asked for access review
evidence, or someone says "prepare the access review", "run the quarterly user recertification",
"who still has admin", "check leavers still have access", "build the access review sheets for
managers" or "our last review was a rubber stamp". Picks the systems in scope, builds account
populations reconciled against HR, pre-flags leavers, orphans, shared and dormant accounts,
assigns independent reviewers, defines the decisions to record, and plans the removal follow-up.

name: agent-acceptance-gate
description: Use when about to commit or push a diff that touches two or more locale variants of one file stem, adds catalog or listing entries, states benchmark numbers, release dates, or licenses for named frontier models, or merges output from any subagent or delegate. Reconciles the lane results, runs the matching preset, and returns PASS, CONDITIONAL PASS, or FAIL with evidence.

name: agent-task-splitter
description: Use when about to run two or more subagents, workflow lanes, or delegated CLI executors on one goal. Gives each lane a role, a pinned model tier, a disjoint file scope, a bounded brief, and a capped return, and fixes the merge and verification step before launch. Not for research-domain routing that owns .research, .paper, Zotero, Obsidian, or NotebookLM workflows; use research-hub-multi-ai for those.

name: AI Services Market MCP
description: Teaches an agent to connect to the AI Services Market MCP server (https://aiservicesmarket.lol/mcp) and use its seven tools — search_skills, get_skill, search_use_cases, get_use_case, get_entitlement, create_checkout, claim_pro — to find installable agent skills, read full details and pricing, and generate Stripe checkout links for single skills or Pro subscriptions. Use when someone asks an agent to find, compare, or buy an AI agent skill.

name: ai-acceptable-use-rules
description:
Use this skill when staff already use AI assistants, coding tools or AI features and the company
needs rules people will follow, and asks "write our AI usage policy", "can staff use ChatGPT",
"generative AI policy", "what data can we put into AI tools", "approved AI tools list", "rules for
AI agents and connectors" or "AI literacy for staff". Finds out what people actually use, sets a
short list of approved tools with a data traffic light, rules for checking outputs and for agents
that act, a fast route to request a new tool, and writes a two-page rule set, the approved tools
list and rollout notes.

name: ai-act-risk-classification
description:
Use this skill when a company must work out where each of its AI systems sits under the EU AI Act,
and asks "is this high-risk", "classify our AI systems", "AI Act risk tier", "are we a provider or
a deployer", "does Annex III apply to us", "is this a prohibited practice", "what does the AI Act
mean for our chatbot" or "which AI Act obligations do we have". Tests each system, one at a time,
for scope, role, prohibited practices, the two high-risk routes, the narrow exemption, transparency
duties and general-purpose models, and writes a reasoned classification record per system plus a
summary table of resulting obligations to confirm with whoever owns legal interpretation.

name: ai-draft-challenge-review
description:
Use this skill when someone is about to sign or approve a GRC artefact an AI agent drafted (a
risk register, applicability statement, policy, impact assessment, audit checklist, corrective
action, scope statement) and asks "how do I review this AI draft", "what should I check before
I sign", "challenge the AI's register", "is this draft actually supported", "fill in the review
record", "how do I avoid rubber-stamping the agent's work" or "what did the AI miss". Gives the
approver a checklist: sample statements back to their cited sources, spot plausible but
unsupported claims, test coverage against the draft's Not checked list and against what it never
mentions, test at least one item the draft did not flag, record every change, and complete the
Review record.

name: ai-impact-assessment
description:
Use this skill when one AI system needs its impact on people and on the company assessed before
launch, after a significant change, or because a customer, auditor or regulator asks for it, and
the team says "AI impact assessment", "assess the impact of this model", "fundamental rights impact
assessment", "who could this AI harm", "bias assessment before launch" or "sign-off for the AI
feature". Describes the system in its context, works through impacts on the people it affects with
evidence, sizes them, proposes mitigations with measurable triggers, and writes one assessment
ready for the system owner and an accountable executive to sign.

name: ai-management-system-scope
description:
Use this skill when a company that already runs a security management system wants to add an AI
management system, or is preparing for an AI governance certification, and asks "scope our AI
management system", "what should the AIMS cover", "AI governance roles", "who owns AI governance",
"extend our ISMS to AI" or "write the AI management system scope statement". Decides which AI
systems, roles, teams and lifecycle stages are in, maps interfaces and dependencies, reuses the
processes the security system already runs, assigns roles with a RACI, and writes the scope
statement, the roles file and the open questions for leadership.

name: ai-system-inventory
description:
Use this skill when a company needs to know what AI it builds, buys or uses, before an AI
governance programme, an AI regulation review or a customer questionnaire, and asks "list our AI
systems", "build an AI register", "AI inventory", "where are we using AI", "find shadow AI",
"which of our vendors use AI" or "what AI do we have before the AI Act". Discovers AI systems from
procurement, single sign-on, code and teams, records one entry per use case with owner, purpose,
data, affected people and the company's role, and writes a CSV register plus notes of borderline
cases and open questions.

name: ai-vendor-due-diligence
description:
Use this skill when the company is about to buy, renew or switch on an AI product or an AI feature
inside an existing product, and asks "assess this AI vendor", "do they train on our data", "AI
supplier questionnaire", "review the AI terms", "can we use this model provider with customer
data", "who are the subprocessors behind this AI tool" or "AI vendor risk assessment". Sizes the
review to the use, reads the terms, data processing agreement and documentation before asking
questions, checks training use, retention, model changes, subprocessors, transfers, security and
exit, and writes an assessment with a recommendation plus the follow-up questions for the vendor.

name: Aider AI Pair Programming CLI Agent
description: Aider is an open-source AI pair programming tool that runs in your terminal, letting you collaborate with LLMs to edit code across your entire codebase. With 42k+ GitHub stars and 15 billion tokens processed weekly, it features deep git integration, repo-wide code mapping, and support for 100+ programming languages.

name: anofox-forecast-detection
description: Seasonality, changepoint, peak, and decomposition detection for the anofox_forecast DuckDB extension. Use when identifying seasonal periods before configuring seasonal forecasting models, detecting structural breaks, analysing peak timing regularity, or decomposing a series into trend / seasonal / residual components.

name: Anyquery Universal SQL Engine with MCP Integration
description: Anyquery is a SQL query engine that lets you run SQL against 40+ apps, files, and databases including GitHub, Notion, Chrome, and Apple Notes. Built on SQLite with MCP server support for connecting AI agents to structured data across services.

name: Audit performance claims with Pstack benchmark-checklist
description: Check tuning, bottlenecks, correctness, repeatability, and end-to-end relevance before an agent reports a measured speedup or regression.

name: auditor-interview-prep
description:
Use this skill when process owners, engineers or executives will be interviewed in an external
or internal audit and need to be ready, or when someone asks "prepare the team for the auditor
interviews", "what will the auditor ask our CTO", "interview briefing for the audit", "how should
people answer the auditor", "mock audit interviews" or "our engineers are nervous about the
audit". Builds a one-page brief per role: what the auditor is likely to ask, the records that
person should be able to open, the honest way to answer what they do not know, and a short
mock interview, plus an interview schedule with the evidence each session needs.

name: auditor-sample-preparation
description:
Use this skill when an external audit, attestation examination or assessment is coming and the
team wants populations and evidence ready for the samples the auditor will pull, or asks
"prepare for audit sampling", "what samples will the auditor ask for", "get our populations
ready", "the auditor wants a list of all changes in the period", "evidence for the leavers
sample", "Type II sample prep" or "how do we prove completeness of the population". Lists the
populations an auditor is likely to sample, builds each from the system of record with the
query that produced it, checks completeness and the evidence behind a dry-run sample, and
writes a readiness file per population plus a list of gaps to fix before fieldwork.

name: AWS MCP Servers for Cloud Service Integration
description: The official AWS Labs MCP server collection provides AI agents with structured access to AWS documentation, service APIs, billing data, and infrastructure metadata through the Model Context Protocol, built and maintained by AWS for secure cloud automation workflows.

name: backup-restore-test-evidence
description:
Use this skill when a restore test is due, an auditor or customer asks for proof that backups can
be recovered, or someone says "plan a restore test", "prove we can recover in time", "our
backups succeed but we never restored", "test our RTO and RPO", "write up the disaster recovery
test" or "document the backup restore for the audit". Picks what to restore, writes a test plan
with success criteria set before the test, records timings against the recovery objectives, and
produces a signed-off test record with the issues found and their owners.

name: bcp-tabletop-design
description:
Use this skill when a company must test its incident response or continuity plan without breaking
anything, because an audit, a customer, a regulator or the plan itself calls for an exercise, and
someone asks "design a tabletop", "run a ransomware tabletop", "BCP exercise", "crisis simulation",
"test our incident response plan", "write the injects" or "we need exercise evidence". Picks two or
three objectives, builds a realistic company-specific scenario with timed injects that force
decisions, briefs the facilitator and observers, and writes the exercise plan, the injects, the
observer sheet and a findings record that ends in owned actions.

name: Bearer CLI SAST Code Security and Privacy Scanner
description: Bearer CLI is an open-source static application security testing (SAST) tool that scans source code to identify, filter, and prioritize security vulnerabilities and privacy risks. Covers OWASP Top 10 and CWE Top 25 with data flow analysis across multiple languages.

name: Bootstrap and verify self-hosted Rakazo from published images
description: Prepare a Docker-based Rakazo installation, preserve private configuration, and verify service health, the selected sandbox, and an optional first bot reply before handoff.

name: business-impact-analysis
description:
Use this skill when a company needs recovery objectives it can defend, before a continuity plan,
a disaster recovery design, an audit or a resilience review, and asks "do a BIA", "business impact
analysis", "set our RTO and RPO", "what is our maximum tolerable downtime", "which services are
critical", "impact tolerance" or "can our backups meet our recovery targets". Lists services from
the customer's view, prices an outage over time in the company's own money and obligations, sets
recovery time and data loss objectives, maps dependencies, and compares each objective with what
backups, restore tests, suppliers and people actually allow, listing the gaps for a decision.

name: change-management-evidence-sampling
description:
Use this skill when an auditor will test change management, or the team wants to know before they
do, and asks "sample our production changes", "check our PR approvals", "do we have segregation
of duties on deploys", "test change management before the audit", "were emergency changes
approved" or "can a developer push to production alone". Builds the change population from what
actually reached production, reconciles it with tickets and pull requests, draws a recorded
sample, tests approval, testing, segregation and emergency attributes, and writes the results and
the exceptions as facts.

name: Chroma MCP Server for Embedding Database Operations
description: An official MCP server for the Chroma open-source embedding database. Enables AI agents to create collections, add documents, perform vector search, full-text search, and metadata filtering through the Model Context Protocol.

name: control-coverage-mapping
description: Use for "which attacker techniques do our controls stop, and how well?", "what controls should I have for this threat?" or "what telemetry detects it?": joins a security control baseline to ATT&CK techniques using 9,545 public control-to-technique mappings from six sources and returns four ranked lists (strong, weak, gaps, unaddressed anywhere). For gap analysis, programme prioritisation, board coverage reporting or FAIR Resistance Strength. Invoke after /threat-actor-profiling or /lookup-liberty91 has produced a technique list.

name: control-owner-raci
description:
Use this skill when controls have no clear owner, or "security" owns everything, and the team asks
"who owns each control", "build a RACI for our controls", "assign control owners", "nobody knows
who runs the access review", "set a review cadence per control" or "the auditor asked who is
accountable". Assigns one accountable role and the operators to every applicable control, checks
workload and segregation of duties, sets a review cadence from how each control runs, and writes a
RACI table plus a one-page brief per owner role.

name: customer-security-questionnaire-answers
description:
Use this skill when a customer or prospect has sent a security questionnaire, due diligence form
or vendor assessment and someone asks "answer this security questionnaire", "fill in the
customer's vendor assessment", "draft answers from our policies", "we have 300 questions due
Friday", "reuse our previous questionnaire answers" or "which answers can we not back up".
Drafts every answer from the company's own documents with a source and a confidence level, flags
answers without evidence and answers that create commitments, checks consistency with past
answers, and writes an answer sheet plus a list of items for owners to confirm.

name: data-subject-request-procedure
description:
Use this skill when a company needs a working process for privacy requests, or just received one
and has none, and asks "DSAR procedure", "how do we handle a subject access request", "someone
asked us to delete their data", "right to erasure process", "data subject rights workflow", "GDPR
request handling" or "we missed the one-month deadline". Designs intake from any channel, a
proportionate identity check, the system search map, review and redaction, response templates per
right, deadline tracking and a request log, written as a procedure the support and privacy teams
can run.

name: Datacircle
description: Every GTM API plan on datacircle.dev, as one file you download and query. LinkedIn profiles, people and company search, find and validate email and phone, company data, jobs and posts, each plan with its price per 1,000, score, rate limits, the fields it returns and its docs. Use it to compare or price a GTM data API.

name: dbt MCP Server for Data Pipeline Context
description: The official dbt MCP Server by dbt Labs provides Model Context Protocol tools for AI agents to interact with dbt projects, query the Semantic Layer, execute SQL, generate SQL from natural language, and explore data model lineage across dbt Core, Fusion, and Platform environments.

name: document-consistency-check
description:
Use this skill when a set of policies, procedures, plans and registers has grown in pieces and
someone asks "check our documents for contradictions", "are our policies consistent", "the
retention periods don't match", "which severity scale is right", "harmonise our ISMS documents",
"cross-check the incident plan against the policy" or "clean up our documentation before the
audit". Extracts the checkable facts from every document (periods, deadlines, scales, roles,
labels, references), finds contradictions, naming drift and broken references, proposes which
document owns each fact, and drafts a glossary and a fix list for the owners.

name: dpa-security-annex-review
description:
Use this skill when a data processing agreement is being negotiated or renewed and someone asks
"review the TOMs annex", "check the security measures in this DPA", "can we sign this annex",
"the customer sent their DPA with a security schedule", "is our standard annex still true" or
"does this vendor's annex promise enough". Breaks the technical and organisational measures annex
into single commitments, compares each one with what the company actually runs or with what the
use case needs, and writes a line-by-line review, proposed redlines and a list of practice gaps
for owners.

name: dpia-screening
description:
Use this skill when a new product feature, vendor, AI use, monitoring tool or change in processing
raises the question "do we need a DPIA", or someone asks "DPIA screening", "is this high risk
processing", "data protection impact assessment threshold", "privacy impact screening for this
feature", "does our AI feature need a DPIA" or "document why we did not do a DPIA". Describes the
processing with numbers, tests it against the GDPR cases, the supervisory authority's list and
the EDPB-endorsed criteria, reaches a reasoned outcome (required, recommended, not required) with
a re-screen trigger, and keeps a screening log for accountability.

name: dust Intuitive Disk Usage Analyzer CLI
description: A more intuitive version of the du command, written in Rust. dust instantly visualizes which directories consume the most disk space using colored proportional bars and smart recursive depth.

name: evidence-freshness-check
description:
Use this skill when an audit, attestation period or customer review is coming and someone asks
"is our evidence up to date", "check the evidence folder before the auditor sees it", "which
screenshots are stale", "do we have evidence for the whole period", "find undated evidence" or
"what will the auditor reject". Indexes every evidence artefact with the date inside it, its owner
and the period it covers, flags what is stale, undated, unowned, outside the audit period or
missing for a recurring activity, and writes an index plus a refresh list per owner.

name: evidence-request-list-builder
description:
Use this skill when an auditor, assessor or regulator has sent a request list and the team asks
"turn the auditor's request list into tasks", "who needs to provide what", "build the evidence
tracker", "split the PBC list by owner", "what exactly do they want for this request" or "we have
two weeks to send everything". Normalises each request into owned, dated tasks naming the exact
artefact, period and source system, separates population requests from sample requests, batches
the clarification questions, and writes a tracker plus one brief per owner.

name: eza Modern File Listing CLI
description: A modern, maintained replacement for the ls command, written in Rust. eza provides colorized output, Git integration, tree views, symlink awareness, and extended attribute support in a single fast binary.

name: fd Fast File Finder CLI
description: A fast and user-friendly alternative to the find command, written in Rust. fd provides intuitive syntax, regex and glob support, colorized output, parallel execution, and automatic .gitignore awareness.

name: first-gap-assessment
description:
Use this skill when a company starts a compliance programme and needs to know how far it is from a
framework, and asks "run a gap analysis", "how ready are we for the audit", "baseline us against
the framework", "what do we have and what is missing", "readiness assessment before we hire an
auditor" or "how long until we can certify". Baselines what exists against the chosen framework
from documents and records, rates each item by evidence rather than opinion, sizes every gap by
effort and audit risk, and writes a gap register plus a prioritised summary with the long-lead
items first.

name: GitHub MCP Server for AI-Powered Repository Management
description: GitHub's official Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that connects AI agents, assistants, and chatbots directly to GitHub's platform. Enables natural language repository management, code search, issue triage, PR automation, and CI/CD workflow intelligence through a standardized protocol.

name: HTTPie CLI API Testing and Debugging Client
description: HTTPie is a modern, user-friendly command-line HTTP client designed for testing, debugging, and interacting with APIs and HTTP servers. It provides an intuitive syntax with formatted and colorized terminal output, built-in JSON support, and session persistence.

name: ict-risk-framework-check
description:
Use this skill when a bank, payment or e-money institution, investment firm, insurer, crypto-asset
service provider or other financial entity in scope of DORA needs to know whether its ICT risk
management setup holds up, or when someone asks "DORA gap analysis", "are we DORA compliant on
ICT risk", "check our ICT risk management framework", "prepare for the supervisor's DORA review",
"does our ISO 27001 ISMS cover DORA" or "audit our Article 6 framework". Confirms the entity type
and whether the simplified regime applies, maps the entity's own documents and records against
the ICT risk management articles, and writes a gap list with owners, evidence and priorities.

name: ict-third-party-register
description:
Use this skill when a financial entity in scope of DORA needs to build or refresh its register of
ICT third-party arrangements, and someone asks "build our register of information", "list our
ICT providers for the regulator", "which providers support critical or important functions",
"refresh the DORA register", "map our ICT contracts to functions" or "where is our provider
concentration". Builds the population of ICT arrangements including intra-group ones, maps each
to the functions it supports, collects the fields a supervisor will ask about, flags
concentration, missing exit plans and contract gaps, and writes a working register with open
questions for function owners.

name: in-your-own-words
description: Restate in your own words what you think the user's goals are and what problem they're trying to solve. Use for /in-your-own-words.

name: incident-response-plan-drafting
description:
Use this skill when a company has no incident response plan, has one copied from a template that
names teams it does not have, or an auditor, customer or insurer asks for it, and the team says
"write our incident response plan", "IR plan", "security incident procedure", "who does what in an
incident", "incident playbooks", "contact tree for incidents" or "our plan failed in the last
incident". Drafts a plan sized to the company with roles and deputies, a severity scale, a contact
tree with an out-of-band channel, one-page playbooks for the likely scenarios, evidence handling and
a notification decision step, plus a one-page quick reference card.

name: incident-severity-triage
description:
Use this skill when something is happening now: an alert, a suspicious login, a ransomware note,
data sent to the wrong customer, an outage that might be an attack, and someone asks "how bad is
this", "classify this incident", "is this a SEV1", "who do we wake up", "is this a breach", "do we
need to notify anyone" or "start the incident log". Classifies the incident on the company's own
scale in minutes, decides who is called and how fast, flags any regulatory or contractual clock,
lists the evidence to preserve, and starts a timestamped triage record that is revisited as facts
change.

name: Install and write Faber Romanus
description: Download the Faber CLI and write Faber Romanus programs using the official agent skill guides (install, English reader spelling, packages, corpus).

name: internal-audit-checklist-from-scope
description:
Use this skill when an internal auditor has one process or area to audit and needs a working
checklist built from the company's own documents, or asks "build an internal audit checklist",
"audit questions for access management", "what do I test in the supplier process", "audit plan
for this area", "how many samples should I take", "internal audit of our data protection
process" or "test our incident process against what the policy says". Turns each commitment in
the company's policies and procedures into a test with a question, a record to inspect, a
sample and a pass criterion, adds framework-specific checks through a lookup, and writes a
checklist file the auditor fills in during fieldwork.

name: internal-audit-programme-planning
description:
Use this skill when a company needs its internal audit programme for the certification or
examination cycle, or asks "plan our internal audits", "internal audit schedule for the year",
"audit programme for the three-year cycle", "who can do our internal audit", "we are too small
for an independent auditor", "readiness audit before the examination" or "which areas do we
audit first". Ranks audit areas by risk, change and past findings, sets how often each is
audited across the cycle, assigns auditors who are independent of what they audit, sizes the
effort, and writes a programme, a coverage matrix and a calendar for leadership to approve.

name: logging-and-monitoring-evidence-pack
description:
Use this skill when an auditor, customer or regulator will ask how security events are logged and
watched, and someone says "prepare logging evidence", "show we monitor alerts", "what do we log
and for how long", "who looks at the SIEM", "prove an alert was handled" or "our monitoring
evidence is just dashboard screenshots". Maps log coverage and retention per system, lists the
alert rules that matter and where they go, traces real alerts end to end with timestamps, and
writes an evidence pack with the gaps stated plainly.

name: management-review-pack
description:
Use this skill when leadership is due to review the security, privacy or AI management system,
or when someone asks "prepare the management review", "management review agenda", "board pack
for the ISMS", "write the management review minutes", "what metrics do we show leadership",
"the auditor wants evidence of management review" or "our management review is a slide nobody
reads". Assembles the facts leadership needs from the registers, audits, incidents and metrics,
frames each agenda item as a decision with options, checks coverage against the framework with
a lookup, and drafts the pre-read, the agenda and minutes with a decision and action log.

name: MetaMCP Unified MCP Server Aggregator and Gateway
description: MetaMCP is an open-source MCP proxy that aggregates multiple MCP servers into a single unified endpoint with a GUI management interface. It supports namespacing, middleware, rate limiting, OIDC authentication, and works with any MCP client including Claude Desktop and Cursor.

name: multi-framework-overlap-map
description:
Use this skill when a company answers to two or more frameworks and is collecting the same evidence
twice, and asks "map our controls across frameworks", "crosswalk between our certification and
our attestation", "can our ISMS cover NIS 2", "unified control framework", "collect evidence once,
use it everywhere" or "what is unique to each framework". Builds one internal control set in the
company's own words, maps each control to the framework references by bare identifier with an
honest match strength, flags what only one framework asks for, and writes a control map plus an
evidence plan where each artefact is collected once.

name: navi Interactive CLI Cheatsheet Tool
description: An interactive cheatsheet tool for the command line that lets you browse through commands and fill in argument values. Written in Rust with fuzzy search, community-maintained cheatsheet repos, and shell integration.

name: nis2-entity-applicability-check
description:
Use this skill when a company needs to know whether the NIS 2 Directive applies to it, and asks
"are we in scope of NIS 2", "are we an essential or important entity", "which country supervises
us", "do we have to register", "a customer says we fall under NIS 2" or "does DORA replace NIS 2
for us". Works through sector, size, the size-independent cases, entity type, jurisdiction and
sector-specific law, entity by entity and member state by member state, and writes a reasoned
applicability memo with the facts each conclusion rests on and what follows from it.

name: nonconformity-root-cause-and-corrective-action
description:
Use this skill when an internal or external audit raised a nonconformity, finding, exception or
observation and the team must answer it, or asks "write the corrective action plan", "root cause
for this audit finding", "respond to the major nonconformity", "CAPA for the auditor", "how do we
close this finding" or "the auditor rejected our corrective action". Separates correction from
corrective action, runs a root cause analysis that stops at a cause the company controls, checks
for the same problem elsewhere, and drafts a response with actions, owners, dates and the evidence
that will prove effectiveness at the next audit.

name: phi-flow-mapping
description:
Use this skill when a covered entity or business associate needs to know where protected health
information lives and moves, or asks "map our PHI", "ePHI inventory", "HIPAA data flow diagram",
"where does patient data go", "PHI flow map for the risk analysis", "which vendors need a BAA" or
"do our logs contain PHI". Traces health data from where it enters, through systems, integrations,
logs, backups and vendors, to where it leaves and is disposed of, records the safeguards that
cover each flow and the business associate agreement behind each external one, and lists the gaps
as input to the security risk analysis.

name: poam-first-draft
description:
Use this skill when assessment findings, scan results or self-assessment gaps have to become a
plan of action and milestones, or the current one is a list nobody updates, and someone asks
"draft the POA&M", "turn the assessment findings into a plan", "put the scan results on the
POA&M", "which POA&M items are overdue", "our milestones just say ongoing", "prepare the POA&M
for the authorizing official" or "plan of action for the gaps from our self-assessment". Builds
one row per weakness with its source, control id, risk, owner role, dated milestones, resources
and status, flags vague milestones and overdue items, and lists the decisions only the named
official can take.

name: policy-gap-review-against-practice
description:
Use this skill when a team suspects its policies describe a company that does not exist, before an
audit or customer review, or asks "do our policies match what we actually do", "check the policy
against reality", "paper versus practice", "will the auditor find gaps in our policies", "our
policy says quarterly but we never do it" or "align policies with how we work". Turns each policy
into testable statements, samples the systems and records that show the practice, classifies every
gap and proposes whether to fix the policy or the practice, with owners and priorities.

name: policy-review-cycle-refresh
description:
Use this skill when the periodic policy review is due or overdue, or someone asks "run the annual
policy review", "our policies are out of date", "re-approve the policies before the audit", "what
changed since the last review", "policy version history" or "who needs to sign off which policy".
Collects what changed since each policy was last approved (incidents, findings, exceptions, new
systems, law), proposes the edits per policy, separates editorial from substantive changes, drafts
the version history and approval record, and plans the communication to staff.

name: post-incident-review
description:
Use this skill when an incident or a serious near miss is closed and the team must learn from it,
or an auditor asks for lessons learned, and someone says "run the post-mortem", "post-incident
review", "lessons learned", "retro on the outage", "blameless review", "root cause of the
incident" or "what do we change after this breach". Builds the timeline from records before the
meeting, runs a blameless discussion, finds the contributing factors, and turns them into a few
owned, dated actions linked to updates of the risk register, controls, playbooks and supplier
records, then writes the review and an action tracker.

name: privacy-and-ai-control-applicability
description:
Use this skill when a company with a security applicability statement extends its management
system to privacy or to AI, and asks "extend our SoA for privacy", "which privacy controls apply
to a processor", "AI controls applicability", "SoA for our AI management system", "are we
controller or processor for this" or "do the AI development controls apply if we only use a
model". Settles the company's role per processing activity and per AI system, decides
applicability of the additional controls from those roles and the risk or impact assessments,
and writes an extension to the applicability statement plus role and scope notes.

name: privacy-notice-gap-check
description:
Use this skill when a published privacy notice may no longer match what the company does, or
someone asks "is our privacy policy accurate", "check our privacy notice against the RoPA",
"privacy notice review", "Article 13 and 14 check", "does our website privacy policy cover our
vendors and cookies" or "update the privacy notice for the new product". Maps every collection
point, compares each notice with the processing record, the vendor list and what the site and
product actually collect, classifies what is missing, wrong, vague or stale, and drafts a redline
plus the practice fixes that a notice edit cannot solve.

name: procs Modern Process Viewer CLI
description: A modern replacement for ps written in Rust. procs provides colorized, human-readable process listings with multi-column keyword search, TCP/UDP port display, Docker container names, and tree views.

name: Qdrant MCP Server for Vector Search and Semantic Memory
description: An official Qdrant MCP server implementation that provides semantic memory capabilities for AI agents. Enables storing and retrieving information using vector search, acting as a persistent knowledge layer on top of the Qdrant vector database.

name: Query isolated Git worktree code maps with ProjectAtlas
description: Register existing Git worktrees under explicit MCP aliases, refresh their separate code maps, and return bounded source evidence across selected checkouts.

name: regulatory-incident-reporting-clock
description:
Use this skill when an incident may have to be reported to an authority, customers or affected
people, and the team asks "do we have to notify", "72 hours", "24 hour early warning", "is this a
notifiable breach", "major incident report", "who do we tell and by when", "draft the breach
notification" or "do we tell the customers". Fixes the facts and the awareness time, tests each
regime and contract that may apply, builds one table of recipients and deadlines with the earliest
first, drafts each notification for review, and records the reasoning for every decision not to
notify.

name: risk-acceptance-memo
description:
Use this skill when a risk owner wants to accept a residual risk instead of treating it further,
or when someone asks "write a risk acceptance", "we want to accept this risk", "risk exception
form", "document the risk acceptance for the auditor", "security exception for this system",
"can we sign off this risk" or "management accepted the risk, how do we record it". Drafts a
one-page decision record per risk: the risk and its score, the options considered with cost, why
acceptance is reasonable, compensating measures with evidence, conditions, expiry and the
triggers that reopen it, with a signature block for the person who holds the authority.

name: risk-method-drafting
description:
Use this skill when a company needs a written risk assessment method before it builds or rescores
a register, or when the current method produces registers where everything scores 3. Triggers:
"write our risk methodology", "define likelihood and impact scales", "what is our risk appetite",
"risk acceptance criteria", "who can accept a risk", "our auditor says the method is not
repeatable", "risk matrix for our ISMS". Drafts a short method with likelihood and impact anchors
in the company's own money, hours and records, a scoring rule, an acceptance threshold with an
authority ladder, reassessment triggers, and a calibration test on five sample risks.

name: risk-register-first-pass
description:
Use this skill when a team needs its first information security risk register, or has one that is
a copied catalogue nobody owns, and asks "build our risk register", "draft a risk assessment",
"what are our top risks", "risk register from scratch", "our auditor wants a risk assessment" or
"turn our incidents and findings into risks". Drafts 20 to 40 company-specific risk scenarios from
the material the agent can reach, scores them against an agreed method, proposes owners and
treatments, and writes a CSV register plus a notes file of assumptions and questions for owners.

name: risk-register-hygiene-review
description:
Use this skill when an existing risk register needs a check before an audit, a management review
or a new owner takes it over, or when someone asks "clean up our risk register", "is our risk
register any good", "review the risk register before the audit", "our risks have not been
updated", "find duplicate risks", "who owns these risks" or "the scores look wrong". Reads the
register read-only and finds stale, duplicated, unowned, orphaned and mis-scored entries, risks
missing given the company's own incidents and findings, and expired acceptances, then writes a
findings file with a proposed fix per line for the owners to decide.

name: risk-to-control-traceability-check
description:
Use this skill when the risk register and the statement of applicability were written separately
and may not agree, and the team asks "do our risks link to our controls", "traceability between
risk treatment and the SoA", "why is this control applicable", "the auditor could not trace a risk
to a control", "check our risk treatment plan against the SoA" or "orphan controls". Checks in both
directions that every treated risk points to controls and actions, and every applicable control
traces back to a risk or obligation, then writes a traceability matrix and a list of orphans and
contradictions with proposed fixes.

name: risk-treatment-plan-drafting
description:
Use this skill when a risk register has treatment decisions but no plan anyone can execute, or
when someone asks "write the risk treatment plan", "turn the risk register into actions", "what
do we do about our high risks", "treatment plan for the auditor", "budget the security roadmap
from the risks" or "our treatment plan is just a list of controls". Turns each reduce, avoid or
transfer decision into dated actions with an owner, budget, dependency and the record that will
prove it was done, states the expected residual score and why, and adds interim measures for
risks that stay high while the work runs. Writes a CSV plan and a short notes file.

name: ropa-first-draft
description:
Use this skill when a company needs its record of processing activities for the first time, or
has one that is really a list of tools, and asks "build our RoPA", "records of processing", "data
map for GDPR", "Article 30 record", "what personal data do we process and why", "data inventory
for privacy" or "our DPO needs a processing register". Drafts the record by processing activity
from systems, vendors and team interviews, with purposes, data and subject categories, proposed
legal bases, recipients, transfers and concrete retention, plus a separate processor record when
the company processes data for customers, and a notes file of open questions per owner.

name: scope-statement-drafting
description:
Use this skill when a team must define what its management system covers before a certification
project, or its current scope is one vague sentence, and asks "write our ISMS scope", "what should
be in scope", "can we exclude the sales office", "scope for the certificate", "draw the boundary of
our management system" or "the auditor says our scope is unclear". Drafts the scope statement with
boundaries, interfaces, dependencies and justified exclusions, for a security, privacy or AI
management system, and writes a statement file plus a boundary table of open questions.

name: secure-development-policy-from-pipeline
description:
Use this skill when an engineering team needs a secure development policy, or has one that does
not match how code really ships, and asks "write our secure SDLC policy", "secure development
policy from our CI", "document our code review and scanning for the audit", "what does our
pipeline already enforce", "change management for engineers" or "secure coding policy for SOC 2 or
CRA". Reads the repositories and pipeline definitions, inventories what is actually enforced
(reviews, checks, scanners, deploy gates, dependency and secret controls), and writes a policy
whose every "must" points to the place it is enforced, with gaps listed as decisions.

name: security-policy-drafting
description:
Use this skill when a company needs its information security policy set written or rebuilt, or
asks "write our security policies", "draft the information security policy", "we need policies
for the audit", "policy pack for a startup", "our template policies are 40 documents nobody reads"
or "which policies do we actually need". Maps the policy set to the company's size and owners,
drafts the top-level policy and the topic policies in testable language that reflects what the
company does, flags commitments that need a decision, and prepares the approval and communication
record for leadership.

name: soa-exclusion-justification-review
description:
Use this skill when a statement of applicability already exists and the team wants its exclusions
to survive the audit, and asks "review our SoA exclusions", "is this a valid justification",
"can we exclude physical security if we are fully remote", "the auditor challenged our not
applicable controls", "rewrite our exclusion justifications" or "we outsource it, so it does not
apply, right". Tests every excluded control against scope, assets, activities, suppliers, risks
and commitments, gives each a keep, rewrite, reverse or ask verdict, and writes a review table plus
rewritten justifications for the owner to approve.

name: soa-first-draft
description:
Use this skill when a company has a risk assessment and treatment plan and now needs its first
statement of applicability, and asks "build our SoA", "draft the statement of applicability",
"which controls apply to us", "SoA from the risk treatment plan", "justify inclusions and
exclusions" or "our SoA says implemented everywhere". Drafts one row per control of the reader's
framework with the inclusion decision, the risk or obligation behind it, an implementation status
taken from records, an evidence pointer and an owner role, and writes a CSV statement plus notes
of open decisions.

name: soa-status-reconciliation
description:
Use this skill when the implementation status column of a statement of applicability may not match
reality, and the team asks "is our SoA accurate", "check the implemented column", "do we have
evidence for every implemented control", "reconcile the SoA with our evidence", "pre-audit evidence
check" or "the auditor found a control marked implemented with no records". Samples the records
behind every control marked implemented, grades the evidence, proposes a corrected status for each
row and writes a reconciliation table plus an evidence gap list with owners.

name: source-provenance
description: Use when you need to know where reporting actually came from: an article URL with "where does this come from?", "who is the original source?", "is this a rewrite?", or another skill needs the provenance chain before grading or citing. Follows links and attributions back to the originating vendor, government, victim or actor document and returns the chain, the primary's access and confidence language, dates and unresolved hops. Deterministic, no API key. Invoked by /quality-of-information-check, /threat-actor-profiling, /campaign-tracking and /intelligence-writing.

name: ssp-control-implementation-statements
description:
Use this skill when a system security plan has to be written, rebuilt or brought up to date
before an assessment, and someone asks "write the SSP", "draft control implementation
statements", "our SSP just repeats the controls", "what is inherited from the cloud provider",
"fill in the customer responsibilities", "get the SSP ready for the assessor" or "which
statements can we actually prove". Drafts one implementation statement per control id from the
reader's own policies, configurations and records (who, what, how, where, how often), marks each
as inherited, hybrid or system-specific, records the parameter values in use, and flags every
statement that is claimed but not evidenced.

name: stage-1-readiness-walk
description:
Use this skill when a certification audit is booked and the team wants to know whether the first
stage will go through, and asks "are we ready for stage 1", "pre-audit readiness check", "what
will the auditor read first", "documentation review before the certification audit", "mock stage
1" or "what would stop the audit". Walks the documentation set the way a certification auditor
reads it, checks that documents agree with each other and with the records, and writes a list of
stoppers, likely findings and polish items with an owner and a fix for each.

name: subprocessor-register-update
description:
Use this skill when the company acts as a processor for its customers and someone asks "update
our subprocessor list", "are we missing subprocessors", "we added a new tool, do we need to tell
customers", "check the public subprocessor page", "where is customer data processed" or "draft the
subprocessor change notice". Finds which suppliers actually receive customer personal data,
compares them with the published list, records purpose, data, locations and transfer basis for

contradicted and evasive, lists the obligations the report puts back on the customer, and writes

and contracts, scores each supplier on data, access and dependency, assigns a tier by the highest

every score.
